project_name: Streamlining Material Discovery - Bayesian Optimization in Thermal Fluid Mixtures
summary: This project, awarded second place, applied BO to the selection of thermal-fluid mixtures for heat-transfer applications, following the pool-based framing used for nanoporous materials\cite{deshwal_bayesian_2021}. Each candidate fluid in an in-house library of several hundred mixtures was described by four thermophysical properties (viscosity, density, thermal conductivity and heat capacity), and the objective was the measured heat transfer coefficient. A Gaussian-process surrogate was driven through an active-learning loop that started from ten randomly chosen fluids and ran 50 acquisitions, repeated over 20 replicates and benchmarked against random sampling. BO located the top-ranked fluid within roughly 25 to 30 acquisitions and plateaued near the library maximum of the heat transfer coefficient after about 10 to 20, whereas random sampling was still tens of ranks short of the optimum and several units below the best achievable value after the full budget; the spread across replicates was also markedly narrower for BO, which the team framed as giving experimentalists a more dependable shortlist. Two tuning studies accompanied the comparison: a screen over kernel families and length scales identified the Matern kernel as the best performer by marginal likelihood, after which a genetic algorithm refined its length scale over 250 generations, and a comparison of acquisition functions found expected improvement slightly ahead of probability of improvement and the upper confidence bound. The underlying property dataset is proprietary and was not released with the code. (No video was submitted; summary prepared from the team's project page, poster, and repository.)
